# StreamingService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: reached with `game:GetService("StreamingService")`
- **Not creatable**: `Instance.new` refuses it

The streamed world's controls (api-design.md §2.1). A world too large to hold is divided into a uniform grid of chunks; this service decides which of them are resident, by distance to the foci a game names. Streaming is a system rather than scene-root state, which is why it is a service and not a property of `Workspace`. The per-frame cost is budgeted in TIME rather than in a count of chunks, because a chunk's cost varies with what is in it.

**Members below are the ones this class DECLARES.** Everything its base
offers is on the base's page, which is what keeps one added member on
`Instance` from being a change to every page here.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the world streams at all. Turning it off FREEZES the current set rather than draining it: nothing new is scheduled and nothing resident is evicted, which is what makes it usable as `hold the world still while I do something`. Evicting while refusing to load would empty the world one ring at a time and leave nothing to come back to. |
| `LoadRadius` | `number` | `1024` | read/write | How far from a focus the engine tries to keep chunks resident, in metres. Best effort: a chunk inside it is wanted, and one outside stays resident until it passes a WIDER ring, because a single radius makes a focus standing on a boundary load and evict the same chunk every frame -- and the symptom of that is not a wrong world, it is a stutter nobody can find. |
| `MinRadius` | `number` | `512` | read/write | The must-have ring, in metres. Everything inside it is guaranteed resident before a focus may advance into it, so the character walks into a world that exists rather than through one that has not arrived. Read `PauseOutsideLoadedArea` for what happens when it has not. |
| `PauseOutsideLoadedArea` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the simulation waits when the minimum ring is not yet resident. A familiar streaming pause, and the alternative is a character falling through ground that has not loaded. It is a pause and not a rollback: the tick simply does not advance. |

## Methods

### `AddFocus(instance: Instance)`

Streams the world around this instance as well. A focus is normally the character or the camera; several are legal and the engine keeps a chunk that any of them wants. An instance with no position in the world is refused, because a focus that cannot be located would silently anchor the world at the origin.

### `LoadAreaAsync(position: vector, radius: number)`

**Yields.** The calling thread parks until it completes.

Yields until every chunk within `radius` of `position` is resident. What a teleport calls before it moves the character, so the destination exists when they arrive. Returns immediately when the area is already loaded, and raises rather than hanging when the world has no chunks there at all.

### `RemoveFocus(instance: Instance)`

Stops streaming around it. Removing the last focus does not unload the world: it stops anything being wanted, and what is resident stays until something wants it gone.

## Events

Every signal here is **deferred** (ADR 0015): a handler runs at the next
drain point, never inside the call that fired it.

### `AreaLoaded(position: vector, radius: number)`

Fires when an area a script asked for has finished loading. Deferred like every signal.

### `InstanceStreamedOut(instance: Instance)`

Fires for each instance that left the world while a script still held a reference to it. Streamed out means REPARENTED TO NIL rather than destroyed, so the handle a script holds still resolves -- it is a husk, and reading it is legal. An instance nothing referenced is simply destroyed and does not fire this.
